counterfactual_missing_items: No primary tumor identified to explain a tumor thrombus
The right atrial mass could represent a bland thrombus rather than tumor
decisive_items: hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow
thrombus extending into the right atrium
response.rationale: R6 directly captures the diagnostic hepatic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari syndrome), which best explains the acute liver failure and clinical picture. R7 describes the right atrial mass but is less specific as a unifying diagnosis.

rejected.why: Hepatorenal syndrome is a complication of the underlying liver disease, not the primary diagnosis.
IVC thrombosis is part of the thrombotic burden but does not capture the hepatic vein involvement central to the presentation.
Append-only completion of R7 that does not add diagnostic specificity beyond the parent candidate.
Append-only completion of R5 that does not address the hepatic vein thrombosis or provide a unifying diagnosis.
